statement:
Let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional simplex, $d\ge2$, of volume $V$ and centroid $g$. Put $m=d+1$, $b=1/m$, $h=d/m$, $\Gamma=h^d$, and $\kappa=dVh^{d-1}$. Write $\lambda_i$ and $\ell_i$ for the barycentric coordinates and their linear parts. Form the six-base hull by placing $T$ at the four binary bases and convex bodies $A_t,C_t\subseteq T$ of volumes $ta,tc$ at $(-1,1),(1,-1)$ respectively, with $a,c>0$ fixed and $t\downarrow0$. Suppose the respective normalized uniform laws $\nu_t,\omega_t$ converge weakly to $\nu,\omega$, and both limits give zero mass to every level set of every $\lambda_i$. Define
$$
J_i=\min_{|s|\le2}\bigl[a\nu\{\lambda_i\ge b+s\}+c\omega\{\lambda_i\ge b-s\}\bigr],
\qquad \bar J=\frac1m\sum_i J_i.
$$
The attained maximum raw mixed closed-halfspace depth on the fiber at $q=(0,0)$ is $D_t^q=\Gamma V+t\bar J+o(t)$. Every maximizing point on that fiber satisfies $y_t=g+tv_*+o(t)$, where the unique $v_*$ solves $\ell_i(v_*)=(J_i-\bar J)/\kappa$ for all $i$. Equivalently $\max_v\min_i[J_i-\kappa\ell_i(v)]=\bar J$, with unique maximizer $v_*$.
title: All-normal partial-tail first variation at the nonanchor six-base fiber
